messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: ACME POC: follow-up + integration plan (post-demo)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment for the POC/trial: 

Summary from today's call:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for ACME's in-app summarization pipeline (low-latency, cost target ~ $0.0008/token).
- Scope: ingestion -> streaming generation -> post-processing; will exercise tool calling for entity enrichment.
- Target dataset: subset of 50k documents, 1k daily active queries during trial.

Proposed success criteria (draft):
1) Latency: median tail latency (p50/p95) under 300ms / 800ms for 512-token requests at 8k context.
2) Cost: average per-request token cost meets the target above for baseline traffic.
3) Quality: automated evals on 200 prompts: >= 90% pass rate on extraction/summary rubric; manual spot-check for edge cases.
4) Reliability: no more than 1% error rate and graceful fallback to smaller model for safety.

Integration plan & ownership (high level):
- Redwood: provide SDK snippet, streaming endpoints, sample tool-calling handler, and integration checklist (attached).
- ACME: allocate a backend engineer (API + auth) and a data owner for evaluation metrics.
- CS/Eng at Redwood (Monica + Dev): 2-week onboarding / sync cadence.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and sign simple MPA.
- Week 1: exchange keys & envs, sandbox test, SDK integration (streaming).
- Week 2-3: run evaluation set, iterate prompts, enable tool-calling flow.
- Week 4: review results and decide on expansion.

Attachments: redwood-poc-success-criteria.pdf, acme-integration-checklist.xlsx (see attached stubs).

Action items / next steps:
- Elena: confirm success criteria + who will own evaluation at ACME.
- Tom: share the contact for your backend engineer.
- Marissa/Monica: schedule kickoff call next week with Dev for API/integration walk-through.

Happy to adjust.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Priya / team —

Thanks for the intro — below are the concrete integration steps and code snippets to get you streaming and tool-calling quickly. I'm also attaching the integration checklist we referenced.

1) Auth & environment
- We can support API keys (sandbox keys in the shared Drive link) or mutual TLS if you prefer. For initial tests API keys are fastest.
- Sandbox host: sandbox-us-east.redwood.internal (or we can do VPC peering).

2) SDK + streaming example (Node)
- Install: npm i @redwood/inference-sdk
- Streaming usage (pseudo):
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
  const stream = client.streamCompletion({ model: "redwood-8k", input: prompt });
  stream.on("token", (t) => process.stdout.write(t));
  stream.on("end", () => console.log("done"));

3) Tool calling (HTTP webhook handler)
- Redwood will include a tool_call object when model decides to call a tool. Example payload: {"tool": "enrichment", "input": {...}}
- Implement a POST /tools/enrichment route that returns JSON with fields: result, confidence, metadata. Example response: {"result": "…", "confidence": 0.96}

4) Error handling / fallbacks
- If streaming disconnects, re-open with last seen KV cache token id. We provide a small helper to fetch KV offsets.

5) Monitoring & evals
- Send evaluation logs to our secure S3 bucket (we'll provide write creds) and we will run batch evals; Monica will coordinate the rubric.

Attachment: acme-integration-checklist.xlsx (checklist with tick boxes for auth, endpoints, monitoring)

If you prefer, I can hop on the kickoff to walk through these snippets.

Thanks,
